title: Redwood November 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership update and company all-hands covering Q4 priorities, Dedicated and Private product updates, performance metrics, hiring plan, recent incident postmortem, and roadmap. Ends with Q&A and concrete next steps around security docs, hiring plan, and customer pilot list.
next_steps: Avery to share Q4 hiring plan and org chart by 2026-12-01
Samir to publish incident postmortem doc and runbook link by 2026-11-30
Jordan to circulate Dedicated pricing example spreadsheet to Sales by 2026-11-29
Marcus to run customer pilot roster update and follow up with contracts team by 2026-11-30
action_items: Avery | Share Q4 hiring plan and org chart | 2026-12-01
Jordan | Send Dedicated pricing spreadsheet to Sales | 2026-11-29
Marcus | Update pilot roster and follow up on contracts | 2026-11-30
Priya | Start candidate search for infra reliability SREs | 2026-12-15
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Kim: Hey everyone, welcome to the November all-hands... um thanks for joining. We're gonna run through a few big updates today, try to keep this to an hour-ish, then open Q&A.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Quick note on time, ops, uh slight audio lag so if you can't hear, flag in chat. Okay next, performance highlights — we've been pushing the runtime kernels and saw a 12% improvement on long-seq generation on A100-ish tests, uh these are internal bench, not final customer numbers.
[00:42] Lena Rodriguez: To add, batching changes plus KV cache optimizations are cutting median token cost by about 18% for our busiest customers, so that's positive. There's also some regressions on very short request latencies which we're tracking.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: Product update — Redwood Dedicated GA roadmap: we're on track for the public launch in late Q1, there are a few workstreams: pricing, autoscale policies, burst capacity, and the console changes for routing policies.
[01:34] Marcus Nguyen: Sales context — customers keep asking about dedicated vs hosted, and we need clearer blockers: the usual SSO/SAML, VPC peering, and audit logs. Pricing examples will help close deals, and Jordan's spreadsheet will be key.
[02:05] Avery Kim: Quick biz snapshot — ARR growth slowed vs last quarter but retention and expansion have improved; churn is down 0.6 points. We had good uptake on embeddings use cases, but gen is still where highest spend is.
[02:45] Speaker 6: question on revenue cadence and ARR math; Avery: we have a longer notes doc, will share to company.
[03:10] Samir Patel: Incident postmortem — last week we had a service degradation for about 45 minutes tied to autoscaler NPE during a deployment; root cause was a config edge-case where the scale-down timer hit while cache eviction was in-flight, which triggered a cascade. We rolled back, added alerting and fixed the race.
[03:45] Lena Rodriguez: Action taken: improved rollout canary, added a safety gate in autoscaler, and an invariant check for KV cache state. We're writing a runbook and will publish to the ops runbooks page.
[04:20] Ava (intern): clapped? no this is transcribed weird, ignore
[04:30] Jordan Lee: Private product — VPC / on-prem roadmap: we shipped the private control plane prototype for two customers in pilot, KMS integrations are working but there are latency considerations for on-prem deployments if customers host control plane far from inference nodes.
[04:55] Marcus Nguyen: Sales asks — encryption at rest/KMS questions keep popping up; we should pin down default modes and provide a short FAQ for customers on SAML, audit logs, and key rotation.
[05:20] Priya Desai: Hiring update — we are opening roles for infra reliability (SRE), product managers, and two senior backend engineers. The candidate funnel is healthy, but we need interviewers; please sign up for panels.
[05:40] Avery Kim: org updates — we're promoting Lina to Head of Customer Success; congrats, and we'll send an announcement. Also reorg in Platform with a focus team on Runtime & Kernels.
[06:00] Rafael Costa: Ops note — cost optimizations from the last quarter trimmed cloud spend by 9% month-over-month; caching and better kernel selection helped. There's more to do with quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize.
[06:35] Jordan Lee: Roadmap highlights — next 90 days: finalize Dedicated GA, finish Private control plane MVP for three pilots, launch Redis-based prefix cache experiment, and roll out auto-fallback policies for overloaded regions.
[07:10] Avery Kim: Questions? we'll do a rapid-fire Q&A, try to keep them short. Please use raise hand or chat.
[07:33] Employee 12: beiing? question: any changes to usage-based pricing? Marcus: no immediate changes, we're exploring tiered discounts for committed Dedicated customers.
[08:05] Employee 9: security question: SOC 2 timeline — what's the ETA? Priya: we aim to complete SOC 2 type II by end of Q2 next year, audit partner lined up.
[08:40] Employee 3: will there be new pricing for embeddings? Marcus: not at the moment, embeddings stay usage-based but bundling options may be introduced for platform customers.
[09:05] Samir Patel: Technical note — kernel selection now picks quantized kernels for most decoder blocks by default on smaller instances, this reduces memory and can lower cost, but watch for small accuracy drop in long-context. We're adding a canary for models flagged as sensitive.
[09:40] Employee 22: question about Private on-prem latency — Samir: depends a lot on control plane placement and networking; options are private control plane in customer's VPC or local control plane plus offline sync, tradeoffs exist.
[10:05] Avery Kim: OK wrapping up, there's an ask to circulate the incident postmortem, hiring plan, and Dedicated pricing spreadsheet. We'll follow up with links in an email.
[10:30] Jordan Lee: Also reminder — demo day next week for product folks, bring a short 5 minute demo if you're shipping something customer-facing.
[10:45] Q&A continues with a few product clarifications and short answers, some crosstalk and audio dropouts.
[11:50] Avery Kim: thanks everyone, we'll post notes. End of all-hands.
